enonce_intro_markdown: Limbe is a sea site resort town in the South West Region of Cameroon. Every year the city of Limbe attracts many tourists, because of its touristic sites like the botanical garden, the slave village and the sea. Limbe is also host to the only oil refinery in Cameroon. For the past 5 years the city has been experiencing severe floods and the quality of drinking water has been greatly affected. Some tourists have also complained about the dirty nature of the beach. They say the beach is becoming very dark in colour and it is also full of debris.

questions.enonce_markdown: Outline six human activities that can be responsible for the pollution of water bodies in Limbe. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Discharge of oil and petroleum waste from the oil refinery**, from oil spills at the terminal and from leaking fuel of boats and ships: it forms oil films on the sea, **darkens the water and the beach** and kills aquatic life.
2. **Release of untreated industrial effluents** (chemicals, heavy metals, hot water) into rivers and the sea by factories and the refinery.
3. **Dumping of domestic and solid waste** (plastics, bottles, tins, refuse) into streams, drains and the sea, which accounts for the **debris on the beach** and blocks drains, adding to the floods.
4. **Discharge of untreated sewage and open defecation**, including wastewater from homes, hotels and the tourist sites, which brings pathogens (cholera, typhoid) and organic matter that causes **eutrophication**.
5. **Agricultural activities**: run-off of **fertilizers, pesticides and herbicides** from plantations and farms into rivers, causing eutrophication and poisoning.
6. **Deforestation and building on river banks, and sand mining**: soil erosion carries silt into rivers and the sea (turbid, dark water), and floods carry rubbish into water bodies.
7. **Washing of clothes, vehicles and motorbikes** and dumping of used oil in or near streams; fishing with poisons or explosives; careless tourists who leave litter on the beach.

(Any six well outlined activities earn 6 marks.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Propose six measures to the Limbe city council to prevent water pollution in Limbe. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Enforce the laws on pollution**: require the refinery and factories to **treat their effluents** before discharge and to have **oil-spill contingency plans** (booms, skimmers), and fine or sanction offenders (polluter pays principle).
2. **Provide sewage collection and treatment plants**, and public toilets with septic tanks, to end open defecation and the discharge of raw sewage.
3. **Organise regular refuse collection**, provide bins on the streets and the beach and a **sanitary landfill or recycling centre**; ban dumping of waste in drains, rivers and the sea.
4. **Build and clean drainage channels and storm-water systems** so that the floods do not carry refuse and sewage into water sources.
5. **Educate and sensitise the population and tourists** (radio, schools, posters, community clean-up days) on the dangers of water pollution and on proper waste disposal.
6. **Regulate agriculture and land use**: control the use of fertilizers and pesticides, forbid cultivation and building on river banks, **plant trees (a vegetation buffer)** along streams and ban sand mining, to reduce erosion and siltation.
7. **Monitor the quality of water** regularly (rivers, wells, the sea, drinking water) and **protect catchment areas and springs**; organise regular beach clean-ups.

(Any six well stated measures earn 6 marks.)

questions.enonce_markdown: What methods of purification can be used by households in Limbe to purify their water? *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Boiling**: boiling the water for at least 5 to 10 minutes kills the disease-causing bacteria, viruses and protozoa (and removes temporary hardness).
2. **Filtration**: passing water through a **sand and charcoal filter, a ceramic candle filter or a clean cloth** removes suspended solids, some microorganisms and, with charcoal, bad taste and colour.
3. **Chemical disinfection (chlorination)**: adding a few drops of **bleach (sodium hypochlorite) or chlorine tablets** and leaving the water for about 30 minutes kills microorganisms.
4. **Sedimentation (settling) and decantation**, with **alum (aluminium sulphate)** to make the suspended particles clump and settle, followed by pouring off the clear water.
5. **Solar disinfection**: clear plastic bottles exposed to the sun for about six hours (ultraviolet radiation and heat kill microorganisms).
6. **Distillation** gives pure water but is rarely used at home.

(Any four, with a short explanation of how each works, earn 4 marks.)

questions.enonce_markdown: What measures can be used to conserve the Limbe Botanical Garden? *[4 marks]* *(6, 6, 4, 4 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Legal protection**: declare it a protected area, prohibit **encroachment, building, logging, hunting, bush fires and the harvesting of plants** inside it, and employ **guards and rangers** to enforce this.
2. **Propagation and replanting**: grow and replant rare and threatened species from seeds and cuttings, keep a **seed bank and a nursery** (**ex situ conservation**), and replace dead or lost trees.
3. **Control pollution, flooding and erosion**: protect the garden from polluted run-off, build drainage and plant vegetation to hold the soil, and remove **invasive alien species**.
4. **Education and funding**: teach visitors, schools and the neighbouring communities the value of the garden (tourism, research, medicinal plants, climate and soil protection); use the **entry fees and donations** for management, and involve the local communities in its care (eco-tourism).
5. **Regulate visitors** (paths, marked trails, waste bins, no picking) and **research and monitoring** of the species present, with records of their numbers.

(Any four well explained measures earn 4 marks.)
